question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{98}$ be a random sample of size $n=98$ from a population with a population mean $\mu =180$ and population standard deviation $\sigma =70.$ Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is greater than $182.$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.0\,$ | $\,0.5279\,$ | $\,0.5319\,$ | $\,0.5359\,$ |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5675\,$ | $\,0.5714\,$ | $\,0.5753\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.6064\,$ | $\,0.6103\,$ | $\,0.6141\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=98,\,\mu =180,\,\sigma =70.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(180,\frac{{70}^{2}}{98}) \\  & ∼N(180,50).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>182).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>182) & =P(Z>\frac{182-180}{\sqrt{50}}) \\  & =P(Z>\frac{\sqrt{2}}{5}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.28)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>0.28) & =1-P(Z<0.28) \\  & =1-Φ(0.28).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.28)=0.6103.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>182) & =1-Φ(0.28) \\  & =1-0.6103 \\  & =0.3897.\end{aligned}
$$
